Issue 07: The Sound of Rooms

32 pages · Edition of 500

Editor's letter

A note on rooms

Every record we press is made somewhere, and the somewhere always gets onto the tape. This issue is about that: a stairwell, a kitchen, a flat with the heating on.

We still print on a two-colour press above the plant and fold every copy by hand on Thursdays. Come and help, or at least read slowly.

Dee Okafor-Lind, editor

03wowflutter · Issue 07

Feature · Low Ceilings, WF-007

The stairwell sessions

Four players, one closed swimming baths and the longest reverb in Leeds.

04Feature

Liner notes · part one

We found the baths in March. Closed since 2011, the water long gone, the stairwell at the back still holding a sound like a held breath. The cello went on the third landing and the violins on the fifth.

Hana, who plays second violin, spent a morning at the roof hatch because she wanted to hear the room answer from above. Nobody wore headphones. If you listen on speakers, you can hear the door.

05Feature

Liner notes · part two

A room is the fifth member of the quartet, and the only one who never misses a rehearsal.

Ife Okoro, cello

06Feature

Roster · 1 of 3

Marl Quartet

String quartet · Leeds

Why record in a stairwell?

A stairwell tells you how long a note lasts, and nobody argues with a stairwell. We stopped fighting the room and tuned to it.

Ines Haverford

Piano and voice · Glasgow

What did the heating have to do with it?

Radiators tick as they cool, in time with nothing at all. Track four is mostly me trying to play along with one.
